contract_plain_english: If X and Y are any two sub-gaussian real random variables on the same probability space, then their product is sub-exponential, with psi_1 norm at most the product of their psi_2 norms. Neither independence nor mean-zero assumptions are required, and the stated constant is exactly 1.

source_evidence.observation: For sub-gaussian random variables X and Y, the source states that XY is sub-exponential and ||XY||_{psi_1} <= ||X||_{psi_2} ||Y||_{psi_2}.

source_evidence.anchor: Proof of Lemma 2.7.7, including display (2.22) and Young's inequality
source_evidence.observation: After unit-psi_2 normalization, the proof combines the two bounds E exp(X^2) <= 2 and E exp(Y^2) <= 2 with |XY| <= X^2/2 + Y^2/2 to obtain E exp(|XY|) <= 2.
The source defines the psi_2 norm by inf {t > 0 : E exp(X^2/t^2) <= 2}.
The source defines sub-exponentiality and the psi_1 norm through exponential integrability of |Z|.

binders: X and Y, real-valued random variables on a common probability space
conclusions: The pointwise product XY is sub-exponential.
definitions_and_conventions: The product XY is pointwise, and all expectations use the common underlying probability space.
implicit_context: The source does not assume that X and Y are independent.
The source does not assume that either random variable has mean zero.
The inequality has exact constant 1 under the book's displayed norm conventions.

details: The product of any two sub-gaussian random variables is sub-exponential.
The psi_1 norm of the product is at most the product of the two psi_2 norms.
No unspecified absolute constant multiplies the right-hand side.
Young's inequality supplies the pointwise exponential-moment bound.

undebatable_constraints: Both X and Y must be sub-gaussian.
The conclusion includes both sub-exponentiality of XY and the quantitative norm inequality.
The right-hand side is exactly ||X||_{psi_2} ||Y||_{psi_2}, with constant 1.
Independence, centering, and symmetry are not hypotheses.
The product is pointwise and the psi_1 norm is applied to XY.
